acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Guest Host Chana Joffe-Walt asks her kids when they first encountered adult fallibility.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc:
A middle schooler really wants to trust the adults have her best interests in mind. But some of the most powerful people at her school begin to make that very difficult.
Talia Richman originally wrote about Madison for The Dallas Morning News.
acts.credits: By Talia Richman; Produced by Chris Benderev; Edited by Bethel Habte
acts.title: See Something, Slay Something

acts.label: Postscript
acts.desc: In Israel and Gaza, children are directly facing the fact that the adults around them cannot protect them.

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
Comedian Gary Gulman on a choice his dad made for him when he was seven years old.
Gary Gulman’s standup show is based on stories in his new book, a memoir called Misfit.
acts.title: Dad’s Big Idea

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc:
There are many kids who do not gradually discover that grown ups don’t have a handle on everything. These kids already know. Miriam Toews’s novel, “Fight Night,” is about a nine-year-old named Swiv who takes care of her grandma and manages her mom’s mental health struggles. Even simple tasks can become complicated, like taking them both on the bus.
